title: Israel expands eVisa-B2 to 50 more nationalities
summary: The Embassy of Israel in Singapore's notice of 28 October 2026 lists 50 additional nationalities for online B/2 e-Visas (plus India and Sri Lanka from the pilot), and the PIBA portal's public pages as of 31 October 2026 present the e-Visa as open to visa-required countries with no pilot restriction shown; the email-verified form itself was not tested, so the pair notes carry that caveat. The 10 exempt nationalities the notice also names keep their exemption plus ETA-IL.
source_name: PIBA - eVisa-B2 information page

title: Lebanon adopts a new entry standard for Syrian nationals
summary: General Security Notice 572 replaces a single tourist route for Syrian passports with a purpose-by-purpose regime at all air, land and sea ports: pre-booked hotel stay, business visit, property ownership, medical treatment, study and family cases each carry their own stay and papers, and work still requires a Labour Ministry permit plus pre-approval. The announcement was confirmed live by 27 October 2026 (GDGS page crawled that day); the text states no separate gazette day.
source_name: Lebanese General Security, Notice 572 (AR)
State Migration Service of Turkmenistan
summary: Turkmenistan's State Migration Service opened an online e-Visa system on 1 October 2026. The portal's document lists no longer include the invitation letter (LOI) that consular tourist visas have always required — but the list of eligible nationalities has not been published, so for now the advance-visa rule still stands and the portal is a channel to watch, not yet a settled route.
title: Turkmenistan launches an e-Visa portal
Colombia's visa exemption for Israel restored
summary: After the 2024-2026 diplomatic break, Colombia's ordinary-passport exemption was restored 1 September 2026 (embassy confirmation reported 3 September); Colombians again travel on ETA-IL for up to 90 days.
source_name: Wikipedia - Visa policy of Israel (current exemption table)

title: Mauritania's visa-free access to Libya restored
summary: Mauritania's ordinary-passport holders are again visa-free for Libya for up to 3 months, restored on 30 August 2026 and back on the Timatic-based exemption table; visa-free entry is limited to landing at Tripoli Mitiga and Misurata airports, and a security letter from the Libyan immigration authorities may be required.
source_name: Visa policy of Libya (Timatic-based table; North Africa News, 4 September 2026)

title: Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam join China's 240-hour transit and Hainan visa-free schemes
summary: From 20 August 2026, citizens of Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam may use China's 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit (the scheme now covers 57 countries) and the 30-day visa-free entry to Hainan (now 61 countries), the National Immigration Administration announced.
source_name: National Immigration Administration — announcement (20 August 2026)

title: Morocco lifts the visa requirement for Albanian citizens
summary: From 15 August 2026, Albanian ordinary-passport holders are visa-free for short stays in Morocco, notified by Morocco's embassy in Rome to Albania's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, implementing the 1 March 2025 joint declaration. The announcement did not state a maximum stay; 90 days is the short-stay ceiling in Morocco's Law No. 02-03 carried in pair data.
source_name: Albania Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs — exemption announcement (August 2026)
South Africa Electronic Travel Authorisation (DHA)
summary: South Africa switched on its Electronic Travel Authorisation for nationals of China, India, Indonesia and Mexico — initially only for air arrivals at OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria airports. The ETA is multiple-entry with stays of up to 90 days. Everyone else still follows the exemption table or needs a visa in advance; there is no visa on arrival.
title: South Africa's ETA goes live for four nationalities
United States makes the visa bond programme permanent for 50 countries
summary: A Department of State Final Rule of 3 August 2026 made the visa bond programme permanent. Nationals of 50 listed countries who are found otherwise eligible for a B-1/B-2 visa must post a refundable bond of USD 10,000, 15,000 or 20,000, set by the consular officer at the interview (the pilot that began on 20 August 2025 used USD 5,000, 10,000 or 15,000). The list is maintained on travel.state.gov and countries can be added on 15 days' notice.
source_name: U.S. Department of State — Countries Subject to Visa Bonds

title: Cairo airport digital visa on arrival
summary: Cairo International Airport begins selling a digital QR visa on arrival (US$36 including a US$6 service fee) via self-service machines and the Visa on Arrival portal, alongside the US$30 paper sticker. The Washington embassy later claims all airports moved to QR from 1 September 2026, against GOV.UK's Cairo-only account — the scope is unresolved.
source_name: GOV.UK — Egypt travel advice

title: Jordan extends prior-approval exemption to families of Syrian investors
summary: The Ministry of Interior announced on 22 July 2026 that spouses and under-18 children of Syrian Chambers of Commerce Premium and First-Class card holders may enter Jordan without prior approval, extending the existing investor exemption to their immediate families.
source_name: Petra — Jordan eases entry rules for families of Syrian investors
Cabo Verde government portal (gov.cv)
summary: Every traveller to Cabo Verde must pre-register on the EASE portal and pay the airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE online). Since 1 July 2026, arriving without proof of pre-registration costs double the TSA at the border. Pre-registration is an immigration formality, not a visa — it changes nothing about who needs a visa.
title: Cabo Verde doubles the airport tax for unregistered arrivals

source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Armenia
summary: A government decree temporarily exempts nationals of 111 countries who hold a valid residence permit from the US, the EU, the Schengen area or a GCC state. The measure runs from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027. It is residence-based, not passport-based — an ordinary passport alone does not qualify.
title: Armenia temporarily exempts residence-permit holders of 111 countries
Japan raises visa fees fivefold
summary: The Cabinet Order on Fees Collected by Consular Officers was amended with effect from 1 July 2026: a single-entry visa now costs approximately ¥15,000 (was ¥3,000) and a multiple-entry visa approximately ¥30,000 (was ¥6,000), the first revision since 1978. Fees are paid in local currency at the mission.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Visa Fees

title: Ireland ends visa-free entry for Nicaragua, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Saint Lucia
summary: Announced by the Minister for Migration on 11 June 2026 and effective 15 June 2026: nationals of Nicaragua, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Saint Lucia now need a visa before travelling to Ireland, for all passport types including diplomatic and service passports, and a transit visa to pass through. A transitional window for travellers who had booked before 15 June 2026 and arrived by 14 July 2026 has ended. The move aligns Ireland more closely with UK and Schengen practice.
source_name: Citizens Information — Visa requirements for entering Ireland

title: Malaysia becomes visa-free for Libya for 30 days
summary: Malaysian ordinary-passport holders are visa-free for Libya for up to 30 days from 8 June 2026, limited to landing at Tripoli Mitiga and Misurata airports, with a possible security-letter requirement. Malaysia's own older visa table still shows Libya as visa-required and has not been updated for this change.
source_name: Visa policy of Libya (Timatic-based table; Libya Herald, 24 June 2026)

title: Japan passes the JESTA enabling law
summary: The amendment to the Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act creating the Japan Electronic System for Travel Authorization (JESTA) passed the Diet on 29 May 2026 (Law No. 32 of 2026). JESTA will require visa-exempt short-stay visitors to obtain online pre-travel authorisation; the Ministry of Justice aims to introduce it in fiscal year 2028, and the law requires a start no later than 31 March 2029. No portal, fee or exact start date exists yet, and nothing is required of travellers in the meantime.
source_name: Zero Illegal Foreign Residents Plan (Ministry of Justice)

title: Canada suspends immigration documents for residents of DR Congo, Uganda and South Sudan
summary: Temporary Ebola measures: visas, eTAs and permits held by residents of the three countries are suspended — even approved documents cannot be used to travel — and affected applications are processed but not finalised. Extended on 28 September 2026 to run until 27 November 2026. The suspension is keyed to residence, not nationality.
source_name: Government of Canada — IRCC notice, 28 Sep 2026
Voyage Togo — official travel platform
summary: A decree adopted by Togo's Council of Ministers on 26 May 2026 exempts nationals of every African state holding a valid passport from entry visas for stays of up to 30 days. Exempt travellers still file a free travel declaration on the Togo Voyage platform at least 24 hours before arrival. Non-African travellers still need the platform's e-Visa in advance — visas on arrival were abolished in 2022.
title: Togo exempts all African nationals for 30 days
Canada extends its conditional eTA to Indonesia and Malaysia
summary: Eligible travellers from Indonesia and Malaysia who fly to Canada may now apply for an eTA instead of a visitor visa, if they have held a Canadian visitor visa in the past 10 years or hold a valid US nonimmigrant visa. Arrival by land or sea still requires a visa. The two countries join 15 others in the conditional-eTA programme.
source_name: IRCC — entry requirements by country
Sri Lanka ETA portal
summary: Under Special Gazette No. 2490/02, Sri Lanka's ETA became free of charge for nationals of 40 countries, on top of the long-standing bilateral free list. The system is unchanged otherwise: everyone applies for an ETA (online, or at the Colombo airport counter) and receives a 30-day double-entry visit pass.
title: Sri Lanka makes the ETA free for 40 countries
China extends Russia's unilateral visa-free entry to the end of 2027
summary: On 20 May 2026 the Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that the unilateral visa-free arrangement for Russian ordinary passport holders (up to 30 days) is extended to 31 December 2027, beyond the end-2026 expiry of the rest of the scheme.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China — regular press conference (20 May 2026)
Saudi Press Agency
summary: The Saudi–Russian mutual exemption agreement took effect on 11 May 2026: ordinary passports of both countries now get 90 days visa-free. The e-Visa portal's eligibility pages lagged behind the announcement, which is why many datasets still show Russia as e-Visa only.
title: Saudi Arabia and Russia switch on mutual visa-free travel
United Kingdom raises the ETA fee to £20 and the visit visa to £135
summary: The Home Office fee uprating of 8 April 2026 raised the ETA fee from £16 to £20 per person and the Standard Visitor visa (up to 6 months) from £127 to £135; long-term visit visas rose to £506 (2 years), £903 (5 years) and £1,128 (10 years). The fees were unchanged in the 8 October 2026 table.
source_name: Home Office immigration and nationality fees, 8 April 2026 (GOV.UK)

title: United Kingdom adds Nicaragua and St Lucia to the visa-national list
summary: Nicaragua and St Lucia were added to the visa-national list by Statement of Changes HC 1691, in force 15:00 GMT on 5 March 2026; ETA eligibility was withdrawn the same day. Nationals who had already been granted an ETA on or before that time and held a confirmed booking could still travel if they arrived no later than 15:00 BST on 16 April 2026.
source_name: Immigration Rules Appendix Visitor: Visa national list (GOV.UK)

title: United Kingdom enforces the ETA scheme in full
summary: From 25 February 2026 carriers must check a traveller's permission to travel before boarding and may be penalised for carrying someone without it (“no permission, no travel”). From the same date most visa nationals granted a visitor visa receive an eVisa only, with no vignette sticker in the passport.
source_name: No permission, no travel: UK set to enforce ETA scheme (GOV.UK news release)

title: Lebanon quadruples visit-visa fees
summary: Under the 2026 Budget Law, General Security raised the visit/tourist entry-visa fee from 500,000 LBP to 2,000,000 LBP on 18 February 2026; work-entry, conversion and sponsor-transfer fees were set to the same 2,000,000 LBP. Port-issued tourist visas themselves stay free — the fee bites on pre-approved/consular visas and on in-country extensions. Old dollar prices still shown on some embassy pages (USD 17/35) are pre-reform leftovers.
source_name: Lebanese General Security, visa types and fees

title: China grants unilateral visa-free entry to Canada and the United Kingdom
summary: From 17 February 2026, ordinary passport holders from Canada and the United Kingdom may enter China without a visa for up to 30 days for business, tourism, family visits, exchange and transit. The arrangement runs until 31 December 2026.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China — Spokesperson's Remarks (15 February 2026)
Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série — Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026
summary: Interior Ministry Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026 (Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série, 23 January 2026) lists 91 nationalities who must hold a visa before travelling — entry, transit and airport stopovers without one are refused. Nationalities on neither that annex nor the exempt table keep the border visa. Holders of EU/EEA, UK, Swiss, Brazilian, Canadian or US residence permits are carved out of the advance-visa duty even if their passport is listed.
title: Cabo Verde moves 91 nationalities to advance-visa-only

source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali
summary: By Foreign Ministry communiqués of 30 December 2025 and 2 January 2026, Mali suspended the entry of US ordinary-passport holders entirely from 1 January 2026, citing reciprocity. The measure is framed as reciprocal and not necessarily permanent; the US embassy's older fee and validity pages predate it and no longer apply.
title: Mali suspends entry for US citizens
United States expands entry suspensions to 39 countries and Palestinian Authority documents
summary: Presidential Proclamation 10998, effective 1 January 2026, fully suspends entry for nationals of 19 countries — the 12 of the June 2025 proclamation plus Burkina Faso, Laos, Mali, Niger, Sierra Leone, South Sudan and Syria — and for anyone travelling on a document issued or endorsed by the Palestinian Authority. It partially suspends entry (immigrant visas and B-1/B-2, F, M and J visas) for nationals of 20 more countries; for Turkmenistan the suspension now covers immigrant visas only. Visas validly issued before the effective dates were not revoked.
source_name: Presidential Proclamation 10998 of 16 December 2025 (Federal Register, 19 December 2025)
Cabinet Resolution No. 855 (Ministry of Justice database)
summary: Cabinet Resolution No. 855 of 31 December 2025 rewrote the stay arithmetic: the 55-country visa-free regime that read as '60 days' now means 30 days within any 60-day period, Gulf-state nationals get 180 days within 360, and EAEU and several bilateral partners sit at 90-in-180. The headline number most datasets show is no longer the operative one.
title: Kyrgyzstan cuts visa-free stays in a New Year's Eve reform

source_name: Agence Nigérienne de Presse (ANP)
summary: An official communiqué of 25 December 2025 announced a complete and indefinite halt to issuing visas to US citizens and to their entry into Niger, citing reciprocity. Unlike a suspension with a review date, no end condition has been published.
title: Niger bars US citizens indefinitely
Russia–Jordan mutual visa exemption in force
summary: Russian ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for Jordan for up to 30 days per visit and 90 days per calendar year for tourism, private visits or short business under the mutual agreement that took effect on 13 December 2025.
source_name: Embassy of Russia in Jordan — mutual visa exemption agreement

title: Algeria grants 14-day visa-free access to Hong Kong SAR passport holders
summary: From 25 November 2025, Hong Kong SAR passport holders may visit Algeria visa-free for up to 14 days, on notification from the Algerian government to the Hong Kong government. Some airline check-in systems were slow to reflect the arrangement. Algeria still publishes no consolidated exemption list; its ordinary-passport exemptions remain a short list (Libya, Malaysia, Mali, Mauritania, Seychelles, Tunisia at 90 days).
source_name: Government of the Hong Kong SAR — visa-free access announcement (25 November 2025)

title: Canada lifts the visitor visa requirement for Qatar
summary: Qatari citizens no longer need a visitor visa for Canada: for air travel they now use an eTA (CAD 7, valid up to 5 years), and no document beyond the passport is needed by land or sea.
source_name: IRCC — entry requirements by country

title: United Kingdom adds Palestine to the visa-national list
summary: Palestine was added to the visa-national list by Statement of Changes HC 1333, following the UK's formal recognition of the state of Palestine in September 2025. Palestinian nationals need a Standard Visitor visa in advance; previously they were covered only as stateless persons or travellers on non-passport documents.
source_name: Explanatory Memorandum to the Statement of Changes HC 1333, 14 October 2025 (GOV.UK)

title: China extends its unilateral visa-free scheme to the end of 2026 and adds Sweden
summary: China extended its unilateral visa-free scheme for 45 countries to 31 December 2026 and added Sweden from 10 November 2025. Ordinary passport holders of the listed countries may enter China without a visa for up to 30 days for business, tourism, family visits, exchange and transit.
source_name: Embassy of China — Notice on Extension of Unilateral Visa-Free Policy (10 November 2025)

title: United Kingdom adds Botswana to the visa-national list
summary: Botswana was added to the visa-national list by Statement of Changes HC 1333, in force 15:00 BST on 14 October 2025; ETA applications closed to Botswanan nationals the same day and a Direct Airside Transit Visa is now also required. A six-week transition for pre-booked ETA holders ran to 15:00 GMT on 25 November 2025.
source_name: Explanatory Memorandum to the Statement of Changes HC 1333, 14 October 2025 (GOV.UK)

title: ESTA fee rises from USD 21 to USD 40
summary: The fee for an ESTA travel authorisation under the Visa Waiver Program rose from USD 21 to USD 40 on 30 September 2025 under the 2025 budget law (Public Law 119-21), with annual inflation adjustments since: USD 40.27 from 1 January 2026 and USD 40.62 from 16 October 2026. An approved ESTA remains valid for two years or until the passport expires.
source_name: U.S. Department of State — Visa Waiver Program (ESTA fee set by CBP under Public Law 119-21)

title: Uzbekistan–Jordan mutual visa exemption in force
summary: Uzbek ordinary-passport holders are visa-exempt for Jordan for up to 30 days under the mutual agreement that took effect on 25 September 2025; previously they used visa on arrival.
source_name: Gazeta.uz — Uzbekistan, Jordan to introduce visa-free stay (MFA statement)

title: China grants unilateral visa-free entry to Russia
summary: From 15 September 2025, Russian ordinary passport holders may enter China without a visa for up to 30 days for business, tourism, family visits, exchange and transit, under China's unilateral visa-free scheme (Russia reciprocated for Chinese citizens in December 2025).
source_name: National Immigration Administration — Unilateral Visa-Free Country List (as at 17 February 2026)
eVisaburkina — official e-Visa portal
summary: A cabinet decision of 11 September 2025 waived visa fees for nationals of all African states. The application itself is still required — Burkinabè visas run through the eVisaburkina portal with central approval — but the fee line for African passports dropped to zero.
title: Burkina Faso waives visa fees for all African citizens
Jordan lifts prior-approval restrictions for Albania and Moldova
summary: The Ministry of Interior page updated on 11 September 2025 records the minister’s decisions lifting prior-approval restrictions on Albanian and Moldovan passports; both now use visa on arrival. The original signing date of the decisions is not published.
source_name: Jordan Ministry of Interior — Restricted and Non-Restricted Countries
Somalia Immigration and Citizenship Agency
summary: From 1 September 2025, all foreign nationals must apply online in advance through Somalia's e-Visa/eTAS portal — the Immigration and Citizenship Agency's launch notice ended walk-up issuance for ordinary passports. The widely publicised waivers for a handful of countries turned out to cover diplomatic and official passports only.
title: Somalia makes the advance e-Visa mandatory for everyone
Latvia introduces a mandatory Electronic Travel Declaration
summary: Since 1 September 2025, third-country nationals who do not hold a Latvian visa or residence permit must submit an Electronic Travel Declaration at eta.gov.lv at least 48 hours before arriving in Latvia, including in transit. Citizens of EU/EEA and Swiss states, NATO and OECD member states and Brazil are exempt by nationality, as are holders of Latvian visas and residence permits. The declaration is not an entry permit: it collects traveller and trip information for the State Threat Prevention Information System and does not change who needs a visa.
source_name: Latvian Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Electronic Travel Declaration

title: Japan exempts Montenegro from visas
summary: Montenegro was added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 1 September 2025, for holders of ICAO-compliant ePassports only, with a stay of up to 90 days.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)

title: China and Malaysia put mutual visa exemption into force
summary: The China–Malaysia mutual visa exemption agreement entered into force on 17 July 2025. Ordinary passport holders of each country may enter the other without a visa for up to 30 days per visit, with total stays capped at 90 days in any 180-day period.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China — Mutual Visa Exemption List (updated July 2026)

title: China and Azerbaijan put mutual visa exemption into force
summary: The China–Azerbaijan mutual visa exemption agreement for ordinary passports entered into force on 16 July 2025, allowing stays of up to 30 days per visit, capped at 90 days in any 180-day period.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China — Mutual Visa Exemption List (updated July 2026)

title: Decision No. 128 in force: 11-group visa fee table, unified land and air port fees
summary: MFA Decision No. 128 (signed 1 July 2025) replaces the old regime: 11 nationality fee groups from free to USD 400 single-entry, the same fees at land borders and airports, all fees paid in cash at the port. The MFA confirmed via SANA on 29 April 2026 that the decision remains unchanged.
source_name: Syria TV

title: Japan exempts Peru from visas
summary: Peru was added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 1 July 2025, for holders of ICAO-compliant ePassports only, with a stay of up to 90 days.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)

title: United States restricts entry from 19 countries (Proclamation 10949)
summary: Presidential Proclamation 10949, effective 9 June 2025, fully suspends the entry of nationals of Afghanistan, Burma, Chad, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Haiti, Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan and Yemen as immigrants and nonimmigrants, and partially suspends entry (immigrant visas and B-1/B-2, F, M and J visas) for nationals of Burundi, Cuba, Laos, Sierra Leone, Togo, Turkmenistan and Venezuela, subject to narrow exceptions.
source_name: Presidential Proclamation 10949 of 4 June 2025 (recited in Proclamation 10998, Federal Register)

title: China grants unilateral visa-free entry to four Gulf countries
summary: From 9 June 2025, ordinary passport holders from Saudi Arabia, Oman, Kuwait and Bahrain may enter China without a visa for up to 30 days for business, tourism, family visits, exchange and transit, under China's unilateral visa-free scheme.
source_name: National Immigration Administration — Unilateral Visa-Free Country List (as at 17 February 2026)

title: Japan exempts Paraguay from visas
summary: Paraguay was added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 1 June 2025, for holders of ICAO-compliant ePassports only, with a stay of up to 90 days.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)

title: China and Uzbekistan put mutual visa exemption into force
summary: The China–Uzbekistan mutual visa exemption agreement entered into force on 1 June 2025. Ordinary passport holders of each country may enter the other without a visa for up to 30 days per visit, with total stays capped at 90 days in any 180-day period.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China — Mutual Visa Exemption List (updated July 2026)

title: China grants unilateral visa-free entry to five Latin American countries
summary: From 1 June 2025, ordinary passport holders from Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Uruguay may enter China without a visa for up to 30 days for business, tourism, family visits, exchange and transit, under China's unilateral visa-free scheme.
source_name: National Immigration Administration — Unilateral Visa-Free Country List (as at 17 February 2026)

title: Ireland ends visa-free entry for Trinidad and Tobago
summary: Effective 12 May 2025, nationals of Trinidad and Tobago need a visa before travelling to Ireland, and a transit visa to pass through an Irish airport or seaport.
source_name: Citizens Information — Visa requirements for entering Ireland

title: Nigeria launches the e-Visa and abolishes visas on arrival
summary: From 1 May 2025 every traveller who needs a visa for Nigeria must obtain an e-Visa at evisa.immigration.gov.ng before travel; the visa-on-arrival system was abolished the same day. The standard short-visit e-Visa (tourism F5A, single-entry business F4A) is valid for 90 days from issuance and allows a single stay of up to 30 days, non-extendable. ECOWAS citizens and Cameroonians and Chadians remain visa-free, and every traveller must file the free electronic Landing Card before arrival.
source_name: Nigeria Immigration Service — Tourism Visa (F5A) page

title: Japan extends its North Korea sanctions for two more years
summary: Japan's Cabinet decided on 8 April 2025 to extend its own sanctions against North Korea for a further two years, to 13 April 2027, keeping in force the ban on the entry of North Korean citizens.
source_name: Extension of Ban on Imports from and Exports to North Korea (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, 8 April 2025)
Namibia MHAISS — Visa Fact Sheet v4
summary: From 1 April 2025 Namibia replaced its long-standing exemption practice with a reciprocity-based system: a short visa-free list (90 days), a long visa-on-arrival list (fees differ for African Union and non-AU nationals), and everyone else on an advance e-Visa. Several nationalities that had entered freely for decades now need a visa.
title: Namibia rebuilds its visa regime on reciprocity

source_name: Liberia Immigration Service — Visa on Arrival portal
summary: Since 11 March 2025, Liberia's visa on arrival exists only as an online pre-approval: apply at least 7 days ahead on the Liberia Immigration Service portal, pay US$102.50, and collect the sticker after biometrics at Roberts International Airport. There is no walk-up arrival visa, and travellers resident in a country with a Liberian embassy must use the embassy instead.
title: Liberia moves its airport visa to mandatory online pre-approval
Ireland ends visa-free entry for Eswatini, Lesotho and Nauru
summary: Effective 10 March 2025, nationals of Eswatini, Lesotho and Nauru must obtain a visa before travelling to Ireland, and a transit visa if transiting. Emergency travel booked before that date was accommodated until 31 March 2025.
source_name: Immigration Service Delivery — Irish visa requirement for nationals of Eswatini, Lesotho and Nauru

title: Iran: special prior authorisation required
summary: Iranian nationals must obtain special prior authorisation before travel and carriers bar boarding without it; Decision No. 128 later sets Iran alone in Group 10 (USD 400 single-entry).
source_name: Syria TV

title: Mauritania makes the e-Visa mandatory and abolishes visas on arrival
summary: From 5 January 2025 every traveller who needs a visa for Mauritania must obtain an e-Visa from the ANRPTS portal (anrpts.gov.mr) before boarding; the walk-up visa on arrival was abolished and Mauritanian embassies have since stopped issuing visas altogether. The fee is paid in cash on arrival (from €40 / $45 for 30 days for Arab and African nationals, €55 / $60 for other nationalities). Eleven nationalities — including Senegal, Mali, Niger, Algeria, Tunisia and Libya — remain visa-free under mutual abolition agreements.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mauritania — visa page

title: Lebanese entry becomes conditional
summary: Lebanese nationals must meet one of four conditions (Syrian-citizen spouse or parent, valid Syrian residence permit, valid third-country residence permit, or an advance consular visa) to enter; the Group 1 fee exemption itself is unchanged.
source_name: Syria TV

title: United Kingdom re-adds Colombia to the visa-national list
summary: Colombia was re-added to the visa-national list by a Statement of Changes in force 15:00 GMT on 26 November 2024 and removed from the ETA list the next day — it had been due to join the ETA scheme on 8 January 2025. Colombian nationals need a Standard Visitor visa in advance; a transition covered pre-booked travel to 24 December 2024.
source_name: Parliamentary written answer, 11 December 2024 (UK Parliament)

title: Jordan lifts prior-approval restriction for Libyan nationals
summary: Libya no longer appears on the Ministry of Interior restricted list; Libyan passports are visa on arrival (30 days, 40 JOD). The restriction was lifted on 29 October 2024, reported at the time as a medical-tourism measure alongside resumed Royal Jordanian service to Tripoli.
source_name: Jordan Ministry of Interior — Restricted and Non-Restricted Countries

title: Ireland ends visa-free entry for South Africa and Botswana
summary: Effective 10 July 2024, nationals of South Africa and Botswana need a visa before travelling to Ireland, and a transit visa to pass through. Holders of South African diplomatic passports remain exempt.
source_name: Citizens Information — Visa requirements for entering Ireland

title: Japan exempts Panama from visas
summary: Panama was added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 1 April 2024, for holders of ICAO-compliant ePassports only, with a stay of up to 90 days.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)

title: Canada reimposes a partial visa requirement on Mexico
summary: Mexico's full visa-free access to Canada ended: most Mexican travellers now need a visitor visa, keeping an eTA option only when flying and only if they have held a Canadian visitor visa in the past 10 years or hold a valid US nonimmigrant visa.
source_name: IRCC — entry requirements by country

title: Kosovo passports gain visa-free access to Cyprus
summary: The EU visa waiver for Kosovo took effect: holders of biometric Kosovo passports no longer need a visa for short stays in Cyprus (up to 90 days in any 180-day period).
source_name: Wikipedia — Visa policy of the Schengen Area

title: Japan exempts Brazil from visas
summary: Brazil was added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 30 September 2023, for holders of ICAO-compliant ePassports only, with a stay of up to 90 days.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)

title: Japan exempts Qatar, conditional on ePassport registration
summary: Qatar was added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 2 April 2023, for holders who have registered an ICAO-compliant ePassport with a Japanese mission (registration valid 3 years or until the passport expires). The permitted stay is 30 days.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)

title: Japan exempts the United Arab Emirates from visas
summary: The United Arab Emirates was added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 1 November 2022, for holders of ICAO-compliant ePassports only, with a stay of up to 90 days.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)

title: Japan exempts Indonesia, conditional on ePassport registration
summary: Indonesia was added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 1 December 2014, for holders who have registered an ICAO-compliant ePassport with a Japanese mission in Indonesia (registration valid 3 years or until the passport expires). The permitted stay is 15 days.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)

title: Japan exempts Thailand and Malaysia from visas
summary: Thailand and Malaysia were added to Japan's visa-exemption list on 1 July 2013, for holders of ICAO-compliant ePassports only (Thailand 15 days, Malaysia 90 days). Travellers without an ePassport must obtain a visa in advance.
source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)
